patch.diff touches 8 files: CHANGELOG.md, rich/_windows_renderer.py, rich/console.py, rich/control.py, rich/segment.py, tests/test_console.py, tests/test_control.py, tests/test_windows_renderer.py. `diff -rq base generated` reports exactly these files (plus .git), so the generated tree matches the patch.
generated/rich/segment.py:52 adds ControlType.SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 and :55-60 widens ControlCode.
generated/rich/control.py:33 registers the escape format in CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT; :152-161 adds Control.title.
generated/rich/console.py:1175-1192 adds Console.set_window_title between set_alt_screen and the is_alt_screen property, inside the Console class.
generated/rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56 adds the legacy dispatch branch.
reference.diff touches the same four modules at the same logical points.
generated/rich/console.py:1175 `def set_window_title(self, title: str) -> bool`, matching the reference signature.
generated/rich/control.py:152 `def title(cls, title: str) -> "Control"`, matching the reference name and parameter.
generated/rich/console.py:1185-1191 returns True when is_terminal (control written) and False otherwise, matching the reference return contract.

generated/rich/segment.py:55-60 adds Tuple[ControlType, str] as a separate union member; the reference widens to Tuple[ControlType, Union[int, str]]. Both are type-equivalent for the new parameter shape.
No touched module adds an import.
rich/console.py:56 already imports Control, so set_window_title depends on control.py through the existing edge.
rich/_windows_renderer.py already imports Tuple, cast, ControlType, and ControlCode, and the new branch reuses them.
Enum member: generated/rich/segment.py:52.
Escape-format registration: generated/rich/control.py:33 (CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT, the dict Control.__init__ dispatches through at base control.py:44-49).
Legacy renderer dispatch: generated/rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56.
All three registration points that the reference uses are present.
The diff adds no packages, requirements, or new third-party imports.
generated/rich/console.py:1189 delegates via self.control(Control.title(title)), which queues the segment in the buffer (console.py:1504-1512).
The buffer is then either rendered as ANSI text by _render_buffer (console.py:1973-1995) or, on legacy Windows, passed unfiltered to legacy_windows_render (console.py:1962-1966).
The Win32 call stays behind the LegacyWindowsTerm wrapper's set_title (rich/_win32_console.py:534-541), so Console never calls the Win32 API directly.

The patch reuses CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT (control.py:33), the classmethod factory style of Control.alt_screen, show_cursor, and clear (control.py:136-151 in base), and the existing elif dispatch chain in _windows_renderer.py:24-56.
No parallel escape path or new dispatch mechanism is introduced.
generated/rich/control.py:33 builds the OSC string the same way as the other control codes.
The transport-specific Win32 call is confined to LegacyWindowsTerm.set_title (rich/_win32_console.py:534), reached only through the renderer.
The title is interpolated without escaping into the OSC payload. The reference does the same, so this is not a candidate-specific regression and is noted under requirement_intent.
Naming: the title classmethod and set_window_title mirror alt_screen and show_cursor naming, and the Google-style docstrings match the surrounding code.
CHANGELOG.md:10-12 adds an Added entry under [Unreleased] in Keep-a-Changelog form, matching the file's structure.
Test names follow the existing test_control_* and test_* patterns (tests/test_control.py:35, tests/test_windows_renderer.py:136, tests/test_console.py:299).

Minor style divergence: tests/test_console.py:301-302 uses pytest.skip, while base tests guard legacy Windows with `if console.legacy_windows: return` (base tests/test_console.py:872, 882, 898). No pytest.skip appears anywhere in base tests. This is an optional implementation choice that reports the skip instead of passing silently, so it is not counted as a failure.
generated/rich/control.py:33 emits "\x1b]0;{title}\x07", identical to the reference format.
generated/rich/console.py:1185-1191 writes the control only when is_terminal and returns True/False, matching the reference contract.
generated/rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56 forwards the title to term.set_title on legacy consoles, matching the reference.
tests/test_console.py:299-305, tests/test_control.py:35-40, and tests/test_windows_renderer.py:136-142 assert the escape output, the Control segment, and the legacy dispatch.

Shared limitations with the reference, not regressions: (a) with TERM=dumb, is_dumb_terminal (rich/console.py:928-937) makes control() a no-op (console.py:1504-1512) while set_window_title still returns True, so the docstring's 'True means the control was written' is inaccurate; (b) the title is not sanitized, so an embedded BEL or ESC can end or inject into the OSC; (c) the legacy path asserts len(title) < 255 (rich/_win32_console.py:540).
